articles.title: "Best take I've ever seen": Jackson Chourio's walk-off hit for Brewers in postseason almost didn't happen
articles.standfirst: The Milwaukee Brewers took a 2-0 series lead over the San Diego Padres in dramatic fashion on Sunday.
articles.summary: The Milwaukee Brewers took a 2-0 series lead over the San Diego Padres in dramatic fashion on Sunday.
articles.body:
The odds were stacked against the Milwaukee Brewers on Sunday. The San Diego Padres went into the bottom of the 9th inning with a 3-2 lead and had the nearly unhittable Mason Miller on the mound. Yet the Brewers found a way.

It took until the final out - in fact, until the final strike. But Jackson Chourio finished the game with a walk-off, two-run single that sent American Family Field into a frenzy. The only reason it even happened was due to what MLB analyst Ben Verlander called possibly " the best take I've ever seen ".

Jackson Chourio somehow held off on Mason Miller's slider after 104 mph fastball with the count at 1-2

Chourio was ahead 1-0 in the count to start the at-bat, only to fall behind 1-2 after a swinging strike and a foul ball. The first three pitches were all high-velocity fastballs: 102 mph, 102 mph, and 104 mph . On the fourth pitch, Miller tried to ring up Chourio with a low slider , but Chourio refused to chase it . On the next pitch, Miller went back to the fastball, and Chourio hit a liner into center field to end the game.

The reason the take on 1-2 was so impressive was that Miller was setting it up with his fastballs . To a hitter, that slider Miller threw starts in the strike zone, only to quickly dip down completely out of it . Chourio appeared to be looking for it.

At 2-2, Chourio was in a much more favorable count. Miller could have gone with a breaking ball again, but he ran the risk of throwing a ball and bringing the count to a full 3-2 . With the bases loaded, that would have been precarious. In the end, Chourio won the at-bat, and the game.

articles.title: Who is Front Row Amy? The Brewers fan that went viral on social media
articles.standfirst: The 58-year-old Milwaukee supporter has attracted national attention simply by attending games and keeping score
articles.summary: The 58-year-old Milwaukee supporter has attracted national attention simply by attending games and keeping score
articles.body:
Every October, millions of baseball fans tune into the MLB playoffs and discover familiar faces sitting behind home plate. Few have become as recognizable as Amy Williams , the Milwaukee supporter affectionately known as Front Row Amy .

The 58-year-old has spent years watching the Milwaukee Brewers from one of the best seats at American Family Field, carefully recording every pitch while television cameras capture her distinctive outfits and enthusiastic reactions.

Yet Williams has never particularly sought the attention. She considers herself an ordinary baseball supporter whose passion for the Brewers unexpectedly turned her into an internet personality.

"I'm just a normal person. I'm just a normal fan like anyone else who really, really loves the Brewers," she told the Milwaukee Journal Sentinel.

Who is Front Row Amy and how did she become famous?

Williams lives in Oshkosh, Wisconsin, roughly 90 minutes from Milwaukee, where she works as an accountant for her family's property management business.

Her baseball obsession began relatively late, in 2007, when she watched the Brewers while recovering from surgery and became fascinated by the sport.

"It was really exciting and I just was hooked from that first game that I watched," Williams recalled.

She purchased season tickets the following year before moving into Section 117, Row 1, Seat 5 in 2011, establishing the routine that eventually made her famous.

Williams typically attends around 40 regular-season games annually, often traveling alone, and uses a specialized scorebook to document pitches, plays and memorable moments.

"It's a huge part of my life," she explained. "I can't imagine not just being a die-hard fan of the Brewers."

Her regular appearances eventually attracted attention from sports radio, national websites and social media, with a Front Row Amy bobblehead even produced in recognition of her popularity.

Why Front Row Amy stepped away from the spotlight

Although Williams initially enjoyed becoming a recognizable figure, the experience changed when online criticism began overshadowing the positive interactions.

"It's not all it's cracked up to be," she admitted, explaining that she eventually closed her Facebook page and website.

She still has more than 31,000 followers on X, although she now prefers maintaining a lower profile and concentrating on the baseball itself.

That passion produced another unforgettable moment on October 4, when Jackson Chourio delivered a walk-off single against the San Diego Padres on Williams' 58th birthday.

"That was amazing. I kind of forgot it was my birthday because I was so focused on the game," she said.

Will Front Row Amy have to change famous nickname?

Williams faces an unexpected adjustment next season because renovations to American Family Field's premium seating will introduce another row directly in front of her usual position.

Although she will retain her existing seat, the change effectively makes it a second-row location, raising the possibility that Front Row Amy could become Second Row Amy.

The adjustment also comes with a substantial ticket-price increase, although Williams remains primarily concerned about maintaining an unobstructed view of the pitchers.

She has witnessed countless memorable Brewers moments, including postseason victories and historic individual performances, and has no intention of abandoning that tradition.

Asked how much longer she plans to keep attending games, Williams offered a characteristically simple response: "As long as I can."

articles.title: Why the Brewers may be the new Dodgers and become MLB’s “superteam”, while the Yankees aren’t far away
articles.standfirst: The Los Angeles Dodgers may have hit their ceiling, perhaps paving the way for the Milwaukee Brewers to take their place.
articles.summary: The Los Angeles Dodgers may have hit their ceiling, perhaps paving the way for the Milwaukee Brewers to take their place.
articles.body:
Heading into the 2026 MLB season , the Los Angeles Dodgers were once again the overwhelming favorites to win the World Series. The team lost only a couple of key players, and added high-profile players like Kyle Tucker and Edwin Diaz . Everything looked ripe for a potential three-peat.

But once the postseason began, the Dodgers didn’t look quite right. They breezed by the Atlanta Braves , but question marks remained. Against the Milwaukee Brewers , the Dodgers’ flaws were exposed. A dominant sweep by the Brewers has analysts wondering if this could be the beginning of Los Angeles’ decline .

In reality, the only way the Dodgers won’t be a perennial contender is if MLB implements a salary cap or limits team spending within a new CBA - the current CBA expires on December 1, 2026 . Even if that doesn’t happen, the Brewers might have already become “the new Dodgers” . Not because of their spending, but instead because of something else.

Brewers, Dodgers, and Yankees considered a tier above all other MLB teams

Following the conclusion of the NLCS, Mike Axisa of CBS Sports has pondered the question of who will be MLB’s next superteam. In his eyes, the three Tier 1 “powerhouse” teams are the Dodgers, Brewers, and New York Yankees . Milwaukee has an advantage over the other two, though.

They have been baseball's best team the last two seasons and almost their entire core is either signed long-term or under team control with little service time. Milwaukee's farm system is also regarded as one of the game's best, if not the best.

While the Dodgers and Yankees could spend like no other teams, the Brewers have the pieces in place to contend for the foreseeable future. And if the new CBA levels the playing field in terms of big spending, Milwaukee could carve out an even bigger advantage over their competition.

articles.title: Milwaukee Brewers vs Tampa Bay Rays H2H: What is their history before the World Series?
articles.standfirst: Milwaukee holds a narrow advantage in the all-time regular-season series against Tampa Bay
articles.summary: Milwaukee holds a narrow advantage in the all-time regular-season series against Tampa Bay
articles.body:
The Milwaukee Brewers and Tampa Bay Rays are preparing to meet in the 2026 World Series, setting up a matchup between two clubs with very different histories but the same ultimate ambition.

Neither franchise has won a World Series championship, meaning the upcoming series will offer a historic opportunity for whichever team comes out on top.

Although both teams have established themselves as consistent postseason contenders in recent years, they have not faced each other particularly often.

Their interleague history is relatively short, making their head-to-head record an interesting reference point before the Fall Classic begins.

According to Baseball-Reference's Stathead database, Milwaukee leads the regular-season matchup with 15 wins to Tampa Bay's 13 across 28 meetings. The Brewers have also scored 104 runs in those games, compared with 79 for the Rays.

That narrow advantage gives Milwaukee the edge on paper, but it does not guarantee anything in a best-of-seven championship series.

The teams have experienced different results across individual seasons, and their most recent meetings show that Tampa Bay remains capable of challenging its National League opponent.

How did the Brewers and Rays perform in their previous meetings?

The two franchises first met during the 2005 regular season, when Tampa Bay was still known as the Devil Rays . Since then, their matchups have generally been limited to occasional interleague series rather than annual rivalries.

One of Milwaukee's strongest performances came in 2022, when the Brewers swept a four-game series against Tampa Bay, winning all four contests.

That result helped shape the overall head-to-head record, although the Rays have had successful stretches of their own in other seasons.

Their recent results have been more closely contested. In 2024, Milwaukee won two of three games, while Tampa Bay reversed that outcome in 2025 by taking two games from the Brewers in their three-game series.

The teams met again at the start of the 2026 campaign, playing three games in Milwaukee between March 30 and April 1. Tampa Bay opened the series with a 3-2 victory, but the Brewers responded by winning the next two games, 6-2 and 8-2.

Milwaukee therefore took the season series by two games to one, adding another small advantage to its historical record ahead of the World Series. The Brewers also held Tampa Bay to three runs or fewer in each of those games.

Those results provide useful context, but the postseason presents a different challenge. A championship series places greater emphasis on pitching rotations, bullpen management, timely hitting and the ability to respond under pressure.

Brewers and Rays enter the World Series with history to make

Milwaukee earned home-field advantage after finishing the regular season with a franchise-record 103 wins and a 59-loss record.

Tampa Bay also enjoyed a strong campaign, finishing 98-64 and securing its place in the American League postseason.

The Brewers then advanced through the National League playoffs, defeating the San Diego Padres before sweeping the Los Angeles Dodgers in the NL Championship Series. Tampa Bay secured its World Series place by beating the Cleveland Guardians in the American League Championship Series.

The contrast between their previous World Series appearances is notable. Milwaukee last reached the Fall Classic in 1982, when the team was still part of the American League.

The Brewers lost a seven-game series to the St. Louis Cardinals and have waited 44 years for another opportunity to compete for the title.

Tampa Bay has reached the championship series twice before, in 2008 and 2020. The franchise lost to the Philadelphia Phillies in five games in 2008 and fell to the Los Angeles Dodgers in six games in 2020.

Consequently, this matchup guarantees that one of the two franchises will move closer to completing its long search for a first championship.

Both teams have earned reputations for building competitive rosters without relying on the biggest payrolls in baseball, making their success particularly significant for smaller-market organizations.

Familiar faces add another layer to the matchup

The World Series also features connections between the two organizations that go beyond their shared regular-season history.

Tampa Bay pitcher Drew Rasmussen was originally selected by the Rays in the 2017 MLB Draft but did not sign at that time. Milwaukee selected him the following year, and he made his major-league debut with the Brewers in 2020.

Rasmussen later became part of the deal that sent shortstop Willy Adames from Tampa Bay to Milwaukee in 2021. That transaction connected two players who would go on to play important roles for their respective clubs.

Another notable connection is Freddy Peralta , who spent several seasons with Milwaukee before becoming a key figure in Tampa Bay's pitching staff. His experience with the Brewers gives the Rays a player familiar with the organization and its approach to the game.

These links illustrate how player development, trades and roster construction have shaped both franchises over time. They also add intrigue to a championship series in which each team will be trying to exploit every possible advantage.

Who has the advantage before the first pitch?

Milwaukee enters the World Series with a better all-time head-to-head record, a 2-1 advantage from the 2026 regular season and home-field advantage for the championship series.

The Brewers will host Games 1 and 2 before the matchup moves to Tampa Bay for Games 3 and 4, with additional games scheduled if required.

However, Tampa Bay's 13 wins in the 28 historical meetings demonstrate that the gap between the teams is relatively small. Their previous encounters cannot fully predict what will happen when the championship is on the line.

The Brewers may have the statistical edge, but the Rays have already shown they can compete with Milwaukee, and their route to the World Series has demonstrated their ability to perform under pressure.

Ultimately, the head-to-head record provides a useful starting point rather than a decisive forecast. With both franchises seeking their first World Series title, the next chapter of their history will carry far greater significance than the 28 regular-season games that came before it.

articles.title: Cigarettes before the game? The Brewers’ strange ritual on their way to the World Series
articles.standfirst: Christian Yelich revealed the unusual tradition Milwaukee’s hitters shared during a season that ended with a championship after 57 years of waiting.
articles.summary: Christian Yelich revealed the unusual tradition Milwaukee’s hitters shared during a season that ended with a championship after 57 years of waiting.
articles.body:
Every team seems to have its own superstitions for dealing with high-pressure moments. Some players follow very specific routines before taking the field, while others rely on small objects or habits to feel ready to compete. In baseball, where superstitions are part of the game’s culture, the Milwaukee Brewers took that idea to another level with a ritual that caught people's attention during their run to the World Series .

The tradition took place before games and was so unusual that Christian Yelich, the team’s captain, decided to reveal what it was like inside the clubhouse. What might seem unthinkable to others eventually became a familiar sight for members of the Milwaukee squad.

The Brewers’ strange pregame ritual

Milwaukee’s hitters would light cigarettes inside the batting cage, which they called rally heaters. The idea behind the tradition was summed up in a phrase that accompanied the ritual: “If we smoke heaters in the cage, we will smoke heaters in the game” .

Yelich described the scene with a comment that gives a glimpse of the atmosphere inside the team’s facilities: “You walk by the cage and see the cigs lit, and you’re like, the boys are ready to rock” .

The sight of lit cigarettes inside the batting cage eventually became associated with the team's preparation. It wasn't a baseball strategy or a guarantee of victory, but rather a shared superstition that became part of the conversations surrounding the Brewers throughout October.

How did their run to the World Series unfold?

The team posted an 11-2 record during October and went on to win the World Series, ending a 57-year wait for its fans .

The road to the championship was not without its challenges. Milwaukee opened the playoffs against San Diego, defeating the Padres 3-1 in the National League Division Series . Jackson Chourio delivered a walk-off single in Game 2, while Garrett Mitchell made a crucial defensive catch in Game 4.

Next came the matchup against the Los Angeles Dodgers. The Brewers swept the series 4-0, eliminating a team that had been looking to capture a third consecutive championship. Brice Turang set the tone with a home run in the opener, while Milwaukee also had to respond to difficult moments, including deficits it overcame in Game 2.

The World Series against Tampa Bay represented the final challenge. Milwaukee won the series 4-1, with its offense producing 25 runs across five games. Even after losing Game 4 in 12 innings, the team bounced back to close out the series. In Game 5, Jacob Misiorowski pitched 5.2 scoreless innings, delivering a performance that helped set the stage for the championship celebration.
